source.title: The Education (Curriculum Minimum Content) Order (Northern Ireland) 2007, Schedule 2

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Listen and respond to a range of fiction, poetry, drama and media texts through the use of traditional and digital resources

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Tell, re-tell and interpret stories based on memories, personal experiences, literature, imagination and the content of the curriculum

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Participate in group and class discussions for a variety of curricular purposes

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Know, understand and use the conventions of group discussion

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Share, respond to and evaluate ideas, arguments and points of view and use evidence or reason to justify opinions, actions or proposals

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Formulate, give and respond to guidance, directions and instructions

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Participate in a range of drama activities across the curriculum

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Improvise a scene based on experience, imagination, literature, media and/or curricular topics

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Describe and talk about real experiences and imaginary situations and about people, places, events and artefacts

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Prepare and give a short oral presentation to a familiar group, showing an awareness of audience and including the use of multimedia presentations

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Identify and ask appropriate questions to seek information, views and feelings

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Talk with people in a variety of formal and informal situations

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use appropriate quality of speech and voice, speaking audibly and varying register, according to the purpose and audience

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Read aloud, inflecting appropriately, to express thoughts and feelings and emphasise the meaning of what they have read

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Recognise and discuss features of spoken language, including formal and informal language, dialect and colloquial speech.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Participate in modelled, shared, paired and guided reading experiences

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Read, explore, understand and make use of a wide range of traditional and digital texts

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Engage in sustained, independent and silent reading for enjoyment and information

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Extend the range of their reading and develop their own preferences

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use traditional and digital sources to locate, select, evaluate and communicate information relevant for a particular task

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Represent their understanding of texts in a range of ways, including visual, oral, dramatic and digital

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Consider, interpret and discuss texts, exploring the ways in which language can be manipulated in order to affect the reader or engage attention

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Begin to be aware of how different media present information, ideas and events in different ways

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Justify their responses logically, by inference, deduction and/or reference to evidence within the text

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Reconsider their initial response to texts in the light of insight and information which emerge subsequently from their reading

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Read aloud to the class or teacher from prepared texts, including those composed by themselves, using inflection to assist meaning

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use a range of cross-checking strategies to read unfamiliar words in texts

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use a variety of reading skills for different reading purposes.

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Participate in modelled, shared, guided and independent writing, including composing on-screen

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Discuss various features of layout in texts and apply these, as appropriate, within their own writing

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Experiment with rhymes, rhythms, verse structure and all kinds of word play and dialect

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Write for a variety of purposes and audiences, selecting, planning and using appropriate style and form

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use the skills of planning, revising and redrafting to improve their writing, including that which they have composed digitally

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Express thoughts, feelings and opinions in imaginative and factual writing

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use a variety of stylistic features to create mood and effect

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Begin to formulate their own personal style

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Create, organise, refine and present ideas using traditional and digital means, combining text, sound or graphics

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Understand the differences between spoken and written language

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Use a variety of skills to spell words correctly

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Develop increasing competence in the use of grammar and punctuation to create clarity of meaning

statements.subject: Language and Literacy
statements.text: Develop a swift and legible style of handwriting.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Processes in Mathematics: Making and Monitoring Decisions
statements.text: Take increasing responsibility for selecting and using the materials and the mathematics required for their work

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Processes in Mathematics: Making and Monitoring Decisions
statements.text: Identify and obtain the information required for a task, suggesting appropriate sources to find the information

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Processes in Mathematics: Making and Monitoring Decisions
statements.text: Plan and organise their work, learning to work systematically

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Processes in Mathematics: Making and Monitoring Decisions
statements.text: Develop a range of strategies for problem solving, looking for ways to overcome difficulties.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Understand mathematical language and use it to discuss their work and explain their thinking

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Compare their ideas and methods of working with others

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Interpret situations mathematically using appropriate symbols or diagrams

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Present information and results clearly.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Recognise general patterns and relationships and make predictions about them

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Ask and respond to open-ended questions and explain their thinking

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Understand and make general statements

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Check results and consider whether they are reasonable.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Understanding Number and Number Notation
statements.text: Count, read, write and order whole numbers

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Understanding Number and Number Notation
statements.text: Develop an understanding of place value up to two decimal places; use this to multiply and divide numbers by 10 and 100

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Understanding Number and Number Notation
statements.text: Estimate and approximate to gain an indication of the size of a solution to a calculation or problem

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Understanding Number and Number Notation
statements.text: Understand and use vulgar fractions, decimal fractions and percentages and explore the relationships between them

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Understanding Number and Number Notation
statements.text: Understand and use negative numbers in context.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Patterns, Relationships and Sequences in Number
statements.text: Explore and predict patterns and sequences of whole numbers; follow and devise rules for generating sequences

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Patterns, Relationships and Sequences in Number
statements.text: Understand and use multiples and factors and the terms prime, square and cube; appreciate inverse operations

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Patterns, Relationships and Sequences in Number
statements.text: Interpret, generalise and use simple relationships expressed in numerical, spatial and practical situations; understand and use simple function machines

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Number: Patterns, Relationships and Sequences in Number
statements.text: Understand that a letter can stand for an unknown number.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Develop strategies to add and subtract mentally

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Know the multiplication facts up to 10 x 10

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Engage in a range of activities to develop understanding of the four operations of number; appreciate the use of brackets; add and subtract with up to two decimal places; multiply and divide decimals by whole numbers; use these operations to solve problems.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Use the four operations to solve problems involving money

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Discuss the value of money, how to keep money safe, ways in which goods can be paid for and the need for budgeting

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Be able to plan and think ahead in terms of saving and spending money; prioritise spending with a limited supply of money; understand how to access best buys

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Discuss foreign currency including the Euro.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Develop skills in estimation of length, ‘weight’, volume/capacity, time, area and temperature

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Appreciate important ideas about measurement, including the continuous nature of measurement and the need for appropriate accuracy

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Understand the relationship between units and convert one metric unit to another; use the four operations to solve problems

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Calculate perimeter and the areas and volumes of simple shapes

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Understand and use scale in the context of simple maps and drawings

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Recognise times on the analogue and digital clocks and understand the relationship between the 12 and 24-hour clocks; use timetables.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Shape and Space: Exploration of Shape
statements.text: Construct a range of regular and irregular 2-D shapes; classify these through examination of angles and sides; recognise line and rotational symmetry; reflect shapes in a line; explore tessellations; name and describe common 2-D shapes; begin to understand congruence in 2-D shapes

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Shape and Space: Exploration of Shape
statements.text: Construct 3-D shapes; investigate the number of faces, edges and vertices on these shapes; name and describe common 3-D shapes; explore the relationship between 2-D and 3-D shapes.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Shape and Space: Position, Movement and Direction
statements.text: Understand the notion of angle in the context of turning; recognise right angles; understand clockwise and anti-clockwise; know the eight points of the compass; use logo to understand movement and turning; be introduced to a programming language and use it to create pictures and patterns and to generate shapes

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Shape and Space: Position, Movement and Direction
statements.text: Develop language associated with line and angle; recognise properties of acute, obtuse and reflex angles; investigate angles in triangles and quadrilaterals; measure and draw angles up to 360°

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Shape and Space: Position, Movement and Direction
statements.text: Use co-ordinates to plot and draw shapes in the first quadrant.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Handling Data: Collecting, Representing and Interpreting Data
statements.text: Collect, classify, record and present data drawn from a range of meaningful situations, using graphs, tables, diagrams and ICT software

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Handling Data: Collecting, Representing and Interpreting Data
statements.text: Explain their work orally and/or through writing and draw conclusions

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Handling Data: Collecting, Representing and Interpreting Data
statements.text: Interpret a wide range of tables, lists, graphs and diagrams; create and interpret frequency tables, including those for grouped data

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Handling Data: Collecting, Representing and Interpreting Data
statements.text: Design and use a data collection sheet; interpret the results; enter information in a database or spreadsheet and interrogate and interpret the results

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.strand: Handling Data: Collecting, Representing and Interpreting Data
statements.text: Understand, calculate and use the mean and range of a set of discrete data.

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Become familiar with and use the language of probability

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Understand possible outcomes of simple random events; understand that there is a degree of uncertainty about the outcome of some events, while others are certain or impossible

statements.subject: Mathematics and Numeracy
statements.text: Place events in order of ‘likelihood’; understand and use the idea of ‘evens’ and know whether events are more or less likely than this.

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Engage with observing, investigating, and responding to first hand experiences, memory and imagination

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Collect, examine and select resource material to use in the development of ideas

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Look at and talk about the work of artists, designers and craftsworkers from their own and other cultures; appreciate methods used in the resource materials and use their appreciation to stimulate personal ideas and engage with informed art making

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Develop their understanding of the visual elements of colour, tone, line, shape, form, space, texture and pattern to communicate their ideas

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Evaluate their own and others’ work and how it was made, explain and share their ideas discuss difficulties and review and modify work to find solutions

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Use a range of media, materials, tools and processes such as: drawing, painting, printmaking, malleable materials, textiles and three-dimensional construction, selecting which is appropriate in order to realise personal ideas and intentions.

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Work creatively with sound by creating musical stories, pictures, patterns, conversations, accompaniments and by investigating ways of preserving the music they have created

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Sing and perform with simple instruments from memory, by ear or from notation to develop vocal and instrumental skills

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Listen and respond to their own and others’ music-making, thinking about, talking about and discussing a variety of characteristics within music that they create, perform or listen to.

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Develop their understanding of the world by engaging in a range of creative and imaginative role play situations

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Explore a range of cultural and human issues in a safe environment by using drama to begin to explore their own and others’ feeling about issues, and by negotiating situations both in and out of role

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Develop a range of drama strategies including freeze frame, tableau, hot seating, thought tracking and conscience

statements.subject: The Arts
statements.text: Develop dramatic skills appropriate to audience, context, purpose and task by exploring voice, movement, gesture and facial expression through basic exploration of a specific role, and by structuring dramatic activity to make meaning clear for a chosen audience.

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: How they and others interact in the world

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: How living things rely on each other within the natural world

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Interdependence of people and the environment and how this has been accelerated over time by advances in transport and communications

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: The effect of people on the natural and built environment over time.

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: How place influences the nature of life

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Ways in which people, plants and animals depend on the features and materials in places and how they adapt to their environment

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Features of, and variations in places, including physical, human, climatic, vegetation and animal life

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Our place in the universe

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Change over time in places

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Positive and negative effects of natural and human events upon place over time.

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: The causes and effect of energy, forces and movement

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Causes that effect the movement of people and animals

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: How movement can be accelerated by human and natural events such as wars, earthquakes, famine or floods

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Positive and negative consequences of movement and its impact on people, places and interdependence.

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: How change is a feature of the human and natural world and may have consequences for our lives and the world around us

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: Ways in which change occurs over both short and long periods of time in the physical and natural world

statements.subject: The World Around Us
statements.text: The effects of positive and negative changes globally and how we contribute to some of these changes.

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.text: Their self esteem, self confidence and how they develop as individuals

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.text: Their management of a range of feelings and emotions and the feelings and emotions of others

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.text: Effective learning strategies

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.text: How to sustain their health, growth and well being and coping safely and efficiently with their environment.

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.strand: Mutual Understanding in the Local and Wider Community
statements.text: Initiating, developing and sustaining mutually satisfying relationships

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.strand: Mutual Understanding in the Local and Wider Community
statements.text: Human rights and social responsibility

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.strand: Mutual Understanding in the Local and Wider Community
statements.text: Causes of conflict and appropriate responses

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.strand: Mutual Understanding in the Local and Wider Community
statements.text: Valuing and celebrating cultural difference and diversity

statements.subject: Personal Development and Mutual Understanding
statements.strand: Mutual Understanding in the Local and Wider Community
statements.text: Playing an active and meaningful part in the life of the community and being concerned about the wider environment.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Participate in activities and physical challenges to learn, understand and continue to develop the core skills of running, jumping and throwing in a co-operative and competitive context using a variety of equipment

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Progress from simple running, jumping and throwing activities towards becoming involved in more difficult personal challenges and through them, improving performance

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Practise running over short and long distances

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Practise jumping for height and distance

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Practise throwing activities for accuracy and distance from a stationary position to a controlled run-up

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Record and analyse personal performance in a variety of ways.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Progress from using simple movements and gestures, towards developing these into a structured, sequenced and co-ordinated set of movements using variables such as space, direction and speed

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Develop their movements progressively individually; in pairs; in trios; small groups; and larger groups.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Develop more effective use of space levels, directions, speed and strength

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Move with increased control, co-ordination and poise, using a variety of actions and gestures which communicate ideas and feelings

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Create, practise and perform movement sequences, using a variety of stimuli and to an audience

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Structure dances with clear beginnings, middles and ends

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Perform a selection of simple folk dances.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Progress from developing individual skills and partner activities and games to suitable small-sided, adapted and mini-games through both co-operative and then competitive play

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Develop control in running, jumping, changing speed, stopping and starting, with and without small equipment

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Improve their skills of handling, hitting and kicking using a variety of equipment and progress from developing individual skills and partner activities and games to suitable small-sided adapted and mini games through both co-operative and then competitive play

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Develop an understanding of, and participate in, small-sided, adapted and mini games.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Extend their body management skills and improve the variety and quality of movement

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Progress from working individually to working in pairs, trios, small groups and whole groups

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Explore, practise and refine a range of movement skills, including travelling, flight, rolling, balancing, transferring weight, including weight on hands, twisting, turning and stretching.

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Develop basic swimming and personal survival skills

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Understand the importance of personal hygiene in relation to pool use

statements.subject: Physical Education
statements.text: Progress from using a swimming aid to developing their confidence and competence in being able to swim without the use of any aids using recognised swimming strokes.
